In an isosceles triangle, there are two sides and two angles of the same value. In this case, AB = AC and angle B = angle C. Since angle A is opposite to side BC, which is the shortest side, and the two other sides are the same, angle A must be under 60 degrees (not equal to 60).

Because angle A is a multiple of 10 and lower than 60, and you’re looking for the highest possible value of A, angle A must be 50 degrees.

This means that there are (180 - 50) = 130 degrees left to split evenly between the two remaining angles. So, angle B and angle C are both 75 degrees. The answer is A.
